scores.claim_text: The F-35 Lightning II is Hexcel's largest defense program, representing less than 25% of revenues in the Defense, Space & Other market segment in 2025.
supports: usaspending shows real Hexcel DoD obligations

M_value.primary_match: F-35 C2D2 (PE 0604840F, Air Force RDT&E Vol III)

scores.interpretation: F-35 RDT&E and Squadron funding is steady through FY26 (~$1.18B FY26 vs $1.23B FY24). HXL's largest defense program is fully funded forward. No J-Book divergence. Materiality test: F-35 = <25% of 39% Defense = <9.75% of total revenue; even if F-35 wobbled it would not be existential. Severity = PASS.

scores.claim_text: Hexcel supplies advanced composites for the Sikorsky CH-53K King Stallion heavy-lift transport helicopter program, characterized as a growth program in 2025.
supports: pentagon_jbook returned NOT_FOUND for CH-53K, CH-53, King Stallion
scores.interpretation: CH-53K is a Navy aviation procurement line (Marine Corps heavy-lift). The corpus covers 410 PEs (DARPA/MDA/SOCOM/OSD/AF/SF RDT&E plus AF Procurement) but Navy aviation procurement P-40 line items are outside the seeded scope. NOT_FOUND here is a coverage gap, not a red flag. Coverage gap noted; severity = UNVERIFIABLE per heuristic #7. HXL also disclosed CH-53K growth alongside Black Hawk drove Engineered Products defense +13.4% YoY — consistent with public Sikorsky production momentum but cannot be J-Book verified.

scores.claim_text: Sikorsky UH-60 Black Hawk wide chord blade program was Hexcel's largest blade program in 2025 and 2024.
supports: pentagon_jbook returned NOT_FOUND for UH-60 Black Hawk and Black Hawk
scores.interpretation: UH-60 Black Hawk is an Army aviation procurement / Multi-Year Procurement line item. J-Book corpus does not seed Army procurement P-40 lines. NOT_FOUND = coverage gap per heuristic #7. Severity = UNVERIFIABLE. Note: contextually the Army FY26 PB is the budget cycle in which UH-60M MYP-X is the relevant decision, and HXL's blade revenue is at risk if the Army caps Black Hawk procurement in FY27+ — but we cannot adjudicate that from the available J-Book slice.

scores.claim_text: Hexcel supplies advanced composites for the Bell-Boeing V-22 Osprey tilt-rotor aircraft program.
scores.interpretation: CV-22 (AF Special Operations variant of V-22) line shows a steep drop from $16.6M (FY24) to $0.653M (FY26) — FUNDED_SHRINKING — the V-22 line is winding down (consistent with end-of-procurement and ground-and-investigate posture). HXL did not name V-22 as a quantified concentration, only as a qualified-platform line. Materiality test: V-22 listed among many programs, not concentrated. Per heuristic #1, FUNDED_SHRINKING → MODERATE_UNDERDELIVERY. The investor-relevant read: V-22 is a sunset program; any forward HXL composites revenue from V-22 is in run-out, but it is not load-bearing for HXL's narrative.

scores.claim_text: Hexcel sees strong demand in the defense and space market as global defense budgets continue to increase, with 2025 Defense, Space & Other sales of $747.0M growing 5.4% YoY driven by helicopters, military aircraft structures, launchers, and satellites.
supports: usaspending.query_dod_contracts → 83 awards, $8.6M total to Hexcel — real but small relative to claimed $747M Defense, Space & Other
pentagon_jbook(contractor_name=Hexcel) → NOT_FOUND (Hexcel not listed as primary contractor in J-Book corpus)
scores.interpretation: HXL is a Tier-2 composites supplier — never a prime, so absence as primary_contractor in J-Book is expected (heuristic #7 — UNVERIFIABLE noise). The $8.6M direct DoD obligations confirms HXL has some direct prime work (carbon fiber raw material orders, DLA materials buys) but the bulk of HXL's $747M Defense revenue flows via Lockheed/Boeing/Sikorsky/RTX subcontracting and will not show up in usaspending under HXL's own name. The structural concern: HXL's 'global defense budgets continue to increase' narrative is partially exposed because two adjacent program lines we COULD test (V-22, NSSL) are SHRINKING, and several launcher/satellite programs are in flux. The defense growth claim is directionally consistent with broader budget tailwinds but is not corroborated at the program level by the J-Book lines we did hit — MODERATE_UNDERDELIVERY on rigor of disclosure (HXL does not name specific PEs it benefits from), not on the truth of the headline.

scores.claim_text: Hexcel composites are used on the Dassault Rafale fighter, Airbus A400M, and Embraer KC-390 military transport aircraft (a European fighter program contributed to 2025 Defense growth).
supports: pentagon_jbook NOT_FOUND for A400M and Rafale — both are non-US programs and outside corpus
scores.interpretation: Rafale (French), A400M (Airbus Defence multinational), KC-390 (Brazilian) are all foreign procurement programs not in the Pentagon J-Book corpus by construction — they appear in French LPM, German BMVg, UK MoD equivalents. NOT_FOUND is expected per heuristic #7. Severity = UNVERIFIABLE. The European-fighter growth tailwind is plausible given known Rafale export momentum but unfalsifiable in this corpus.

scores.claim_text: Space applications for Hexcel composites include solid rocket booster cases, fairings, and payload doors for launch vehicles, and satellite bus/solar arrays. Launchers and satellites contributed materially to 2025 Defense, Space & Other growth.

M_value.primary_match: National Security Space Launch Program (PE 1206853SF, Space Force)

scores.interpretation: NSSL R&D line shows steep decline from $156.97M (FY24) to $6.6M (FY26) — FUNDED_SHRINKING — consistent with NSSL transitioning from R&D phase into procurement (Phase 3 LSA awarded; the RDT&E line is winding down while the procurement line scales). However, HXL claimed 'launchers' as a 2025 growth driver. If the R&D side of national security launch is going to near-zero in FY26 and procurement awards are concentrated among SpaceX/ULA primes (not HXL direct customers), the composite-content tailwind for HXL on launchers is concentrated in commercial launch (SpaceX Starship, Vulcan upper stage composites) more than in DoD-funded space-launch growth. Per heuristic #1, FUNDED_SHRINKING → MODERATE_UNDERDELIVERY. Caveat: this is one of multiple space programs; we did not query the full SBIRS/SDA Tracking/T2/T3 set.

scores.claim_text: Hexcel says no other defense program (apart from F-35) accounts for more than 10% of revenues in the Defense, Space & Other market.
supports: Statement is a negative/concentration disclosure not testable by pentagon_jbook directly; tested implicitly via F-35 being FUNDED_STEADY and no obvious second concentration
scores.interpretation: Diversification claim is self-consistent with the program-by-program inquiry: F-35 dominates, other programs are individually small. No single shrinking program is large enough to violate the <10% concentration claim. Severity = PASS for the concentration disclosure itself.

scores.claim_text: Hexcel's principal Defense customers include Boeing, Lockheed Martin, General Dynamics, RTX, Textron, GKN, GE as significant counterparties.
supports: Customer list is a long-standing public counterparty disclosure, consistent with HXL's role as Tier-2 advanced-composites supplier across primes. No basis to challenge in J-Book corpus.
scores.interpretation: Control claim. The customer list is consistent with HXL's manufacturing-facility-tied named customers (per ITEM 2 Properties). Severity = PASS.
